source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: EXPLANATIO PRIMI CAPITULI : ANNO TERTIO REGNI JOAKIM REGIS JUDA.
1.title_en: Explanation of the first chapter: In the third year of the reign of Joakim king of Juda.

paras.t: Anno tertio regni Joakim regis Juda, venit Nabuchodonosor rex Babylonis Jerusalem, et obsedit eam. Quarto libro Regum et secundo Paralipomenon patet, quemadmodum Josias rex sanctus tres habuerit filios, qui vitiose et impie post patrem se habuerunt, propter quod capti sunt. Nam primum eorum nomine Joachaz cepit Nechao Pharao rex Ægypti, et fratrem ejus Eliacim pro eo constituit regem, mutans nomen ejus, et Joakim eum appellans. Hic Joakim favit regi Ægypti, a quo promotus fuit, contra Nabuchodonosor regem : idcirco rex Babylonis fecit sibi hunc Joakim tributarium, qui in hac subjectione tribus annis permansit. Postea rebellavit, tuncque protinus Nabuchodonosor venit contra Jerusalem, obsidens eam et vincens.
paras.en: [[1:1|In the third year of the reign of Joakim, king of Juda, Nabuchodonosor, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem, and beseiged it|Anno tertio regni Joakim regis Juda, venit Nabuchodonosor rex Babylonis Jerusalem, et obsedit eam]]. It is plain from the fourth book of Kings and the second of Paralipomenon how Josias, the holy king[[4 Kings 22:1||]][[4 Kings 22:2||]][[2 Par 34:1||]], had three sons[[1 Par 3:15||]] who behaved wickedly and impiously after their father[[4 Kings 23:32||]][[4 Kings 23:37||]][[4 Kings 24:17||]][[4 Kings 24:19||]], for which they were taken captive. For the first of them, Joachaz by name[[4 Kings 23:30||]][[2 Par 36:1||]], was taken by Nechao Pharao king of Egypt[[4 Kings 23:33||]], who set up his brother Eliacim as king in his place, changing his name and calling him Joakim[[4 Kings 23:34||]]. This Joakim favoured the king of Egypt, by whom he had been raised up, against King Nabuchodonosor: therefore the king of Babylon made this Joakim his tributary, and he remained in this subjection for three years. Afterwards he rebelled[[4 Kings 24:1||]], and at once Nabuchodonosor came against Jerusalem, besieging it and conquering it.

paras.t: Unde quod dicitur, In anno tertio regni Joakim, intelligendum est de annis quibus tributarius fuit regis Babylonis, non de tempore illo quo in Jerusalem regnare exorsus est. Undecim quippe annis in Jerusalem regnavit, et quarto anno regni sui cœpit Nabuchodonosor regnare in Babylone, juxta illud Jeremiæ : Verbum Domini quod factum est ad Jeremiam in anno quarto Joakim filii Josiæ regis Juda (ipse est primus annus Nabuchodonosor regis Babylonis). Unde, secundum Hieronymum et Albertum, Joakim octavo regni sui anno, tradidit se potestati Nabuchodonosor, qui fuit quartus annus regni Nabuchodonosor regis. Tertio autem anno post hoc, scilicet undecimo anno regni sui, Joakim rebellavit, et sicut secundo Paralipomenon legitur, ductus fuit in Babylonem. Quod videtur contrariari ei quod Jeremias prædixit, eum projiciendum extra portas Jerusalem, et ibi sepultura asini sepeliendum. Ad quod respondent doctores, quod rex Babylonis eum remisit, inito fœdere pacis. Eo ergo occiso, et sicut Isaias prædixit sepulto, fecit filium ejus regem pro eo : qui filius dictus est Joakin; sed in Hebræo litteris scribuntur diversis. In Latino quoque, primus Joakim ultimam litteram habet m, secundus n. Uterque insuper dictus est Jechonias, ut patet Matthæi primo, quum dicitur : Josias genuit Jechoniam, etc. Itaque primus Joakim trinomius fuit : nam dictus est Eliacim, Joakim, Jechonias; et de isto jam sermo est, non de filio ejus, qui non nisi tribus mensibus regnavit, quibus expletis, a servis Nabuchodonosor captus, atque in Babylonem perductus est.
paras.en: So what is said, [[1:1|In the third year of the reign of Joakim|In anno tertio regni Joakim]], is to be understood of the years in which he was tributary to the king of Babylon, not of the time when he began to reign in Jerusalem. For he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem[[4 Kings 23:36||]], and in the fourth year of his reign Nabuchodonosor began to reign in Babylon, according to that word of Jeremias: [[Jer 25:1|The word that came to Jeremiah|Verbum Domini quod factum est ad Jeremiam]] [[Jer 25:1|in the fourth year of Joakim the son of Josias king of Juda, (the same is the first year of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon|in anno quarto Joakim filii Josiæ regis Juda (ipse est primus annus Nabuchodonosor regis Babylonis]]) [Denis reads "The word of the Lord" and leaves out "concerning all the people of Juda"]. Hence, according to Jerome and Albert, Joakim in the eighth year of his reign gave himself up to the power of Nabuchodonosor, which was the fourth year of King Nabuchodonosor's reign. And in the third year after this, that is, in the eleventh year of his reign, Joakim rebelled, and, as we read in the second book of Paralipomenon, he was led away into Babylon[[2 Par 36:6||]]. This seems to go against what Jeremias foretold, that he would be cast out beyond the gates of Jerusalem and buried there with the burial of an ass[[Jer 22:19||]]. To this the doctors answer that the king of Babylon sent him back, having made a treaty of peace with him. So when he had been slain, and buried as Isaias had foretold [so the print; the prophecy just mentioned is Jeremias's], he made his son king in his place[[4 Kings 24:6||]]: and this son was called Joakin; but in Hebrew the names are written with different letters. In Latin too the first Joakim has *m* for his last letter, the second *n*. Both, moreover, were called Jechonias, as is plain from the first chapter of Matthew, where it is said: [[Matt 1:11|Josias begot Jechonias|Josias genuit Jechoniam]], etc. So the first Joakim had three names: he was called Eliacim, Joakim and Jechonias; and it is of him that we are now speaking, not of his son, who reigned only three months[[4 Kings 24:8||]], at the end of which he was taken by the servants of Nabuchodonosor and brought away into Babylon[[4 Kings 24:15||]].

paras.t: Quemadmodum autem hoc loco scribit B. Hieronymus, Porphyrius volens Matthæum evangelistam falsitatis arguere, eo quod una generatio desit (ut apparet Porphyrio) in tertia tessaradecade seu quaterdena genealogiæ Christi, imperitiam suam ostendit, putans utrumque Jechoniam seu Joakim esse eumdem.
paras.en: Now, as Blessed Jerome writes on this place, Porphyry, wishing to convict Matthew the evangelist of falsehood because (as it seemed to Porphyry) one generation is missing in the third *tessaradecade* or set of fourteen in the genealogy of Christ, showed his own want of skill, thinking that the two Jechoniases, or Joakims, were the same man.

paras.t: Et tradidit Dominus in manu ejus, scilicet Nabuchodonosor regis, Joakim regem Juda, primum scilicet Joakim, et partem vasorum domus Dei, videlicet templi. Apteque dicitur, Tradidit Dominus, ad insinuandum quod divina voluntate ac potestate, non adversariorum propriis viribus, facta sit ista punitio. Deus quippe per impios sæpe punit iniqua agentes etiam fideles. Unde loquitur Jeremias : Iste novissimus Nabuchodonosor rex Babylonis exossavit eum, scilicet populum Juda; et in Job asseritur : Terra data est in manus impii.
paras.en: [[1:2|And the Lord delivered into his hands|Et tradidit Dominus in manu ejus]], that is, of King Nabuchodonosor, [[1:2|Joakim, the king of Juda|Joakim regem Juda]], that is, the first Joakim, [[1:2|and part of the vessels of the house of God|et partem vasorum domus Dei]], namely of the temple. And it is fittingly said, [[1:2|the Lord delivered|Tradidit Dominus]], to suggest that this punishment was brought about by the will and power of God, not by the enemies' own strength. For God often punishes through the wicked those who do evil, even the faithful. Hence Jeremias says: [[Jer 50:17|last this Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon hath broken his bones|Iste novissimus Nabuchodonosor rex Babylonis exossavit eum]] [the margin gives Jer. i, 17; the words are from Jer 50:17], that is, the people of Juda; and in Job it is said: [[Job 9:24|The earth is given into the hand of the wicked|Terra data est in manus impii]].

paras.t: Et asportavit ea per suos ministros, in terram Sennaar. Terra Sennaar est Chaldæa sive Babylonia, in qua erat campus Duran, ubi filii Adæ turrim Babel construere inceperunt : qui locus dictus est Babel seu Babylon, propter linguarum confusionem ibi peractam, prout in Genesi fertur. Babylon nempe interpretatur confusio. In eodem quoque campo postea constructa est civitas Babylon, et de turre illa ibi incepta, constructum est Capitolium, secundum Hieronymum. Hic ait Albertus : Ejusdem loci nomen est Sennaar, et Duran, ac Babylon. Itaque, Asportavit ea in terram Sennaar, in domum dei sui, id est fanum seu templum idoli quod colebat, et vasa intulit in domum thesauri dei sui. Juxta proprietatem seu consuetudinem idiomatis Hebræorum, vas appellatur quidquid alicujus est contentivum, seu instrumentum ad aliquid peragendum : sicque hoc loco vasa templi Dei feruntur, ea quibus sacerdotes legis in Dei obsequio utebantur. Domus quoque thesauri dei regis Nabuchodonosor dicitur, locus fani in quo pretiosa quæque et quorum usus fuit in cultu idolorum, reponebantur.
paras.en: [[1:2|and he carried them away|Et asportavit ea]] through his ministers [[1:2|into the land of Sennaar|in terram Sennaar]]. The land of Sennaar is Chaldea or Babylonia, in which was the plain of Duran, where the sons of Adam began to build the tower of Babel[[Gen 11:2||]]: this place was called Babel or Babylon because of the confusion of tongues brought about there, as is told in Genesis[[Gen 11:9||]]. For Babylon means *confusion*. On the same plain the city of Babylon was afterwards built, and from that tower begun there the Capitol was built, according to Jerome. Here Albert says: Sennaar and Duran and Babylon are names of the same place. So: [[1:2|he carried them away into the land of Sennaar, to the house of his god|Asportavit ea in terram Sennaar, in domum dei sui]], that is, to the shrine or temple of the idol he worshipped, [[1:2|and the vessels he brought into the treasure house of his god|et vasa intulit in domum thesauri dei sui]]. According to the property or usage of the Hebrew idiom, anything that holds something, or any instrument for doing something, is called a *vessel*: and so here the vessels of the temple of God are the things which the priests of the law used in the service of God. And the treasure house of King Nabuchodonosor's god is the place in the shrine where all the precious things, and those used in the worship of idols, were laid up.

paras.t: Dicunt demum hic aliqui, quod Nabuchodonosor iste fecit aliquam reverentiam Deo cœli, qui in Jerusalem colebatur : quia a templo ejus non abstulit omnia vasa ministerii ejus, imo quædam ibidem ad cultum ejus reliquit : et rursus, quoniam ea quæ abstulit, non usibus applicavit humanis, quemadmodum Balthasar rex nepos ejus, propter quod infra punitus describitur; sed posuit ea in loco secundum suam æstimationem solenni ac sacro, ut dictum est.
paras.en: Lastly, some say here that this Nabuchodonosor showed some reverence to the God of heaven who was worshipped in Jerusalem: because he did not take away from His temple all the vessels of His ministry, but left some there for His worship; and again, because he did not put the things he took away to human uses, as did King Balthasar his grandson[[Dan 5:2||]][[Dan 5:3||]], for which, as is told below, he was punished; but he placed them in a place which in his own estimation was solemn and sacred, as has been said.

paras.t: Quocirca quæri posset, unde pro tunc Nabuchodonosor habuerit notitiam Dei Judæorum. Ad quod poterit responderi, quod vel ex aliorum relatu, vel ex naturali ratione aliqualiter novit unum esse Deum altissimum, sicut et multi gentilium. Etenim plebs Hebræa fuit famosa, et magnalia Dei ejus opera longe ac late etiam in gentilibus innotuerunt, ut patet primo Regum, et in libris Esther ac Judith. Propter quod Jeremias ait in Threnis : Non crediderunt reges terræ quod ingrederetur hostis per portas Jerusalem. Denique ut habetur quarto Regum, per mirabilia quæ circa Ezechiam regem operatus fuit Deus, notitia ejus regi quoque Babylonis, qui ante hunc Nabuchodonosor fuit, innotuit.
paras.en: So it might be asked how Nabuchodonosor at that time came to have knowledge of the God of the Jews. To this it can be answered that, either from the report of others or by natural reason, he knew in some way that there is one most high God, as many of the gentiles also did. For the Hebrew people was famous, and the great works of its God became known far and wide even among the gentiles, as is plain from the first book of Kings[[1 Kings 4:8||]][[1 Kings 6:5||]][[1 Kings 6:6||]] and from the books of Esther[[Esth 6:13||]] and Judith[[Jdt 5:1||]]. That is why Jeremias says in Lamentations: [[Lam 4:12|The kings of the earth, and all the inhabitants of the world would not have believed, that the adversary and the enemy should enter in by the gates of Jerusalem|Non crediderunt reges terræ quod ingrederetur hostis per portas Jerusalem]] [Denis's shorter wording leaves out "and all the inhabitants of the world" and "and the enemy"]. Finally, as we have in the fourth book of Kings, through the wonders God worked concerning King Ezechias, the knowledge of Him reached the king of Babylon too who was before this Nabuchodonosor[[4 Kings 20:12||]][[2 Par 32:31||]].

paras.t: Et ait rex Nabuchodonosor Asphanez præposito eunuchorum. Secundum Albertum, eunuchus dupliciter dicitur : primo, ab accidente corporis, scilicet quia exsectus seu castratus ; secundo, ratione obsequii. Antiquorum namque mos fuit servos habere eunuchos sive castratos : propter quod consuetudo inolevit, servos vocare eunuchos. Hinc ait Lyra : Antiquitus qui in domo regis serviebant ad interiora domus, castrabantur propter securitatem a mulieribus, ut aliqui dicunt. Alii vero affirmant, quod dicebantur eunuchi propter castitatem et morum honestatem, propter quod servitores generaliter eunuchi vocati sunt. Unde in Actibus vocatur eunuchus potens vir ille, qui erat super omnes gazas Candacis reginæ Æthiopum. Quomodo autem præsenti loco nomen eunuchi sumatur, non penitus certum est, aliis dicentibus quod primo modo, aliis quod modo secundo. Horum itaque eunuchorum Asphanez fuit præpositus seu magister.
paras.en: [[1:3|And the king spoke|Et ait rex]], Nabuchodonosor, [[1:3|to Asphenez, the master of the eunuchs|Asphanez præposito eunuchorum]]. According to Albert, *eunuch* is said in two ways: first, from a condition of the body, namely because a man has been cut or castrated; secondly, by reason of service. For it was the custom of the ancients to have eunuchs, that is, castrated men, as servants: hence the custom grew up of calling servants eunuchs. So Lyra says: In ancient times those who served in the king's house in its inner rooms were castrated, for safety with regard to the women, as some say. Others, however, affirm that they were called eunuchs because of their chastity and the uprightness of their conduct, and that for this reason servants in general were called eunuchs. Hence in the Acts that powerful man who was over all the treasures of Candace queen of the Ethiopians is called a eunuch[[Acts 8:27||]]. In which way the name of eunuch is taken in the present place is not altogether certain, some saying in the first way, others in the second. Of these eunuchs, then, Asphanez was the master or overseer.

paras.t: Ut introduceret de filiis Israel aliquos, præclariores videlicet, et de semine regio, qui essent de genere David famosissimi regis : de quo et gentilium historiographi conscripserunt ; et tyrannorum pueros. Tyranni uno modo dicuntur, qui potentia abutuntur et voluntatem habent pro ratione. Alio modo, qui in regni negotiis strenui sunt : sicque in libro Esther et hoc loco sumuntur. Propter quod dicit Albertus : Tyranni hic appellantur, non a corruptione regni atque regiminis, sed potius a strenuitate rei militaris. Unde Hieronymus dicit, quod tyranni hoc loco sunt nobiles. Nobiles equidem, strenuitate animi et rei militaris exercitio, regibus sunt necessarii : propterea Plato in primo Timæi ad rem militarem eligi præcipit electam juventutem. Electa vero juventus vocatur, quæ corporis robore ac mentis præminet strenuitate. Hinc Nabuchodonosor jussit pueros tales in suum palatium introduci : hi enim facilius informantur. Nobiles quoque induci præcepit, quoniam tales coram regibus stare ministrareque solent : qui etiam ex superbia ignobiles spernere consueverunt. Insuper nobiles interdum ad informationem magis dispositi sunt : etenim nobilium est nobile cor habere, juxta illud Isaiæ : Princeps ea quæ digna sunt principe, cogitabit, et ipse super duces stabit. Boetius quoque secundo de Consolatione philosophiæ testatur, quod nobilitas est laus quædam proveniens homini de probitate parentum. Idcirco in generis nobilitate hoc bonum est, quod per ipsam quædam necessitas nobilibus imponitur, ne a majorum suorum probitate degenerent. Secundum hoc homines bene morigerati et originati, ad sapientiam asseruntur dispositi, quia sedatis passionibus anima eruditur, dicente Philosopho, Anima quiescendo fit prudens.
paras.en: [[1:3|that he should bring in some of the children of Israel|Ut introduceret de filiis Israel]] some, namely the more illustrious, [[1:3|and of the king's seed|et de semine regio]], that is, those who were of the line of David, that most famous king, of whom the historians of the gentiles also wrote; [[1:3|and of the princes|et tyrannorum]] [literally "of the tyrants"; Denis goes on to explain the word] [[1:4|Children|pueros]]. *Tyrants* are so called in one way when they abuse their power and have their will in place of reason; in another way, when they are vigorous in the affairs of the kingdom: and so the word is taken in the book of Esther[[Esth 6:9||]] [where the Douay-Rheims has "nobles" for *tyrannis*] and in this place. That is why Albert says: They are called tyrants here not from the corruption of a kingdom and its government, but rather from vigour in warfare. Hence Jerome says that *tyrants* in this place are nobles. Nobles indeed, by vigour of spirit and practice in warfare, are necessary to kings: therefore Plato in the first book of the *Timaeus* directs that a chosen youth be picked for warfare. And a chosen youth is one that excels in strength of body and vigour of mind. Hence Nabuchodonosor ordered such boys to be brought into his palace: for these are more easily formed. He also ordered nobles to be brought in, because such men are wont to stand and minister before kings; and they, moreover, are wont out of pride to despise the lowborn. Besides, nobles are sometimes better disposed to be taught: for it belongs to the noble to have a noble heart, according to that saying of Isaias: [[Is 32:8|the prince will devise such things as are worthy of a prince, and he shall stand above the rulers|Princeps ea quæ digna sunt principe, cogitabit, et ipse super duces stabit]]. Boethius too, in the second book of the *Consolation of Philosophy*, testifies that nobility is a certain praise that comes to a man from the uprightness of his parents. So this is the good in nobility of birth, that through it a certain necessity is laid on the noble not to fall away from the uprightness of their forebears. Accordingly men of good character and good birth are said to be disposed to wisdom, because the soul is taught when the passions are calmed, as the Philosopher says: The soul becomes prudent by being at rest.

paras.t: In quibus nulla esset macula, id est defectus membri sive deformitas. Reges enim, pulchros atque adspectu delectabiles volunt habere ministros : ideo subditur, decoros forma, per venustatem coloris, ut scilicet essent elegantis dispositionis in quantitate membrorum, et proportione eorum ad invicem, ac superfusione candidi cujusdam coloris. Ex his enim pulchritudo corporis, secundum Augustinum in libro de Civitate Dei, resultat. Tales quoque solent esse ad sapientiam aptiores. Dicit enim Philosophus : Monstrum in corpore, frequenter est monstrum in mente. Commentator quoque super Ethicam scribit : Indicia virtutum animæ relucent in corpore, sicut in vivacitate sensuum prudentia ; in debita proportione membrorum, mensuræ et quantitates justitiæ ; in complexione æquali, temperantia ; et in robore corporis, animi fortitudo. Hinc et de Christo fuit prædictum : Speciosus forma præ filiis hominum. Tales etiam decori, frequenter affatu dulcissimi sunt.
paras.en: [[1:4|in whom there was no blemish|In quibus nulla esset macula]], that is, no defect of limb or deformity. For kings wish to have handsome ministers, pleasing to look upon: therefore it is added, [[1:4|well favoured|decoros forma]] [literally "comely of form"], by grace of colouring, that is, that they should be of an elegant make in the size of their limbs and their proportion to one another, and with a certain fair colour spread over them. For from these, according to Augustine in the book *Of the City of God*, the beauty of the body arises. Such men too are usually more apt for wisdom. For the Philosopher says: A monster in body is often a monster in mind. And the Commentator on the *Ethics* writes: The signs of the soul's virtues shine out in the body: prudence in the liveliness of the senses; the measures and quantities of justice in the due proportion of the limbs; temperance in an even complexion; and fortitude of soul in strength of body. Hence it was foretold of Christ too: [[Ps 44:3|Thou art beautiful above the sons of men|Speciosus forma præ filiis hominum]]. Such comely men are also often most pleasant of speech.

paras.t: Et eruditos omni sapientia. Secundum Albertum (per quem in toto hoc opere intelligo Albertum Magnum, ordinis Prædicatorum, Ratisbonensem episcopum), eruditus, est extra rude imperitiæ positus. Dicitque Boetius, quod eruditi viri est, de quolibet, sicut est, reddere rationem. Sapientia autem est de altissimis quæ difficile est homini scire, et quam propter se ipsam potissime volumus noscere, ut ait Philosophus. Unde in Job habetur : Trahitur autem sapientia de occultis. Et Philosophus : Sapientia, inquit, est divina possessio. Denique reor, quod Nabuchodonosor rex voluerit ut pueri Hebræi coram se introducendi, essent in lege sua instructi. Omnium enim gentium linguas atque scientias voluit sciri ab aliquibus ministrorum suorum, ut tempore opportuno sibi in his deservirent. Hincque hoc loco nomine sapientiæ, notitiam legis ac Prophetarum intelligo.
paras.en: [[1:4|and skilful in all wisdom|Et eruditos omni sapientia]]. According to Albert (by whom throughout this work I mean Albert the Great, of the Order of Preachers, bishop of Ratisbon), *eruditus* [learned, skilled] is one placed outside the rawness of ignorance [Latin *e-rudis*, "out of the raw state"]. And Boethius says that it belongs to a learned man to give an account of anything as it is. Wisdom, moreover, concerns the highest things, which are hard for man to know, and which we most of all wish to know for their own sake, as the Philosopher says. Hence in Job we have: [[Job 28:18|but wisdom is drawn out of secret places|Trahitur autem sapientia de occultis]]. And the Philosopher says: Wisdom is a divine possession. Lastly, I think that King Nabuchodonosor wished the Hebrew boys who were to be brought before him to be instructed in their own law. For he wished the languages and sciences of all nations to be known by some of his ministers, so that they might serve him in these at the proper time. And so in this place I take the name of wisdom to mean knowledge of the Law and the Prophets.

paras.t: Cautos scientia, id est prudentes in rebus humanis. Cautio quippe solet pars poni prudentiæ, per quam homo circumspecte et consulte se habet, oculumque mentalem longe ac late circumducens, ut agat ea quæ non tantum licent, sed et expediunt. Circa quod scribit Albertus : Scientia est effectus demonstrationis, quia scientia in cautelis syllogismorum et probationum consistit. Propter quod dicit, Cautos scientia. Et quia humana ratio de humanis ratiocinatur, asserit Augustinus quod scientia est de humanis, sapientia de divinis. Tales autem cautelas ad respondendum et obviandum necesse est habere curiales, qui frequenter sunt judices : quibus ad recte judicandum necessaria exstat scientia. Nam et de Christo omnium judice Dominus ait in Isaia : In scientia sua justificabit ipse servus meus multos.
paras.en: [[1:4|acute in knowledge|Cautos scientia]] [literally "wary in knowledge"], that is, prudent in human affairs. For wariness is usually counted a part of prudence, by which a man conducts himself circumspectly and with counsel, casting the eye of his mind far and wide, so as to do the things that are not only lawful but also expedient. On this Albert writes: Knowledge [*scientia*] is the effect of demonstration, since knowledge consists in the safeguards of syllogisms and proofs. That is why it says: [[1:4|acute in knowledge|Cautos scientia]]. And since human reason reasons about human things, Augustine asserts that knowledge is of human things, wisdom of divine. Courtiers, who are often judges, must have such safeguards for answering and meeting objections: for to judge rightly they need knowledge. For of Christ too, the judge of all, the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 53:11|by his knowledge shall this my just servant justify many|In scientia sua justificabit ipse servus meus multos]] [Denis's text lacks "just"].

paras.t: Et doctos disciplina. Quemadmodum super illud ad Hebræos, Omnis quidem disciplina, dicit Glossa, duplex est disciplina : Una est morum eruditio, de qua in Proverbiis scribitur : Qui abjicit disciplinam, despicit animam suam ; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, possessor est cordis. Alia est demonstrabilium. Et utroque modo hic sumitur, ut scilicet moribus essent ornati, et disciplinis liberalibus eruditi. Disciplina quoque interdum accipitur pro justa correctione. De qua ad Hebræos ait Apostolus : Quod si extra disciplinam estis, ergo adulteri, et non filii, estis : quis enim filius quem non corripit pater? Et in Proverbiis legitur : Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias : quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit. — Postremo, quoniam philosophia dividitur in naturalem, rationalem, moralem : quidam per sapientiam intelligunt philosophiam naturalem; per scientiam autem, rationalem; per disciplinam vero, moralem.
paras.en: [[1:4|and instructed in science|Et doctos disciplina]] [*disciplina*, "discipline", means both instruction or learning and correction; the Douay-Rheims renders it variously as "science", "instruction", "chastisement" and "correction"]. As the Gloss says on that verse to the Hebrews, [[Heb 12:11|Now all chastisement|Omnis quidem disciplina]], discipline is twofold. One is the training of conduct, of which it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 15:32|He that rejecteth instruction, despiseth his own soul: but he that yieldeth to reproof, possesseth understanding|Qui abjicit disciplinam, despicit animam suam ; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, possessor est cordis]]. The other is of things that can be demonstrated. And it is taken here in both ways: that is, that they should be adorned with good conduct and learned in the liberal disciplines. *Discipline* is also sometimes taken for just correction. Of this the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:8|But if you be without chastisement|Quod si extra disciplinam estis]], [[Heb 12:8|then are you bastards and not sons|ergo adulteri, et non filii, estis]]: [[Heb 12:7|For what son is there whom the father doth not correct?|quis enim filius quem non corripit pater?]] And in Proverbs we read: [[Prov 3:11|My son, reject not the correction of the Lord|Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias]]: [[Prov 3:12|For whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth|quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit]]. Lastly, since philosophy is divided into natural, rational and moral, some understand by *wisdom* natural philosophy, by *knowledge* rational philosophy, and by *discipline* moral philosophy.

paras.t: Et qui possent stare in palatio regis, id est idonei essent manere ac ministrare coram Nabuchodonosor rege. His etenim insigniti, regali adspectu sunt digni. Et id spectat ad regum ac principum prælatorumque laudem, ut taliter eruditos curent secum habere, quorum consilio dirigantur : siquidem quo pluribus præsunt, et plura agere habent, eo plus peritorum egent suffragio. Nam et in Tobia habetur : Consilium semper a sapiente perquire.
paras.en: [[1:4|and such as might stand in the king's palace|Et qui possent stare in palatio regis]], that is, that they should be fit to remain and minister before King Nabuchodonosor. For those marked by these gifts are worthy of the royal presence. And it is to the praise of kings, princes and prelates that they take care to have men so learned about them, by whose counsel they may be guided: since the more people they rule and the more they have to do, the more they need the help of skilled men. For in Tobias too we have: [[Tob 4:19|Seek counsel always of a wise man|Consilium semper a sapiente perquire]].

paras.t: Ut doceret eos præfatus eunuchorum præpositus per se ipsum, vel potius per alios sibi subjectos, litteras, id est scientias, et linguam Chaldæorum. Litteræ autem Chaldæorum maxime erant de scientiis divinativis, secundum Albertum. Itaque Nabuchodonosor voluit secum habere quosdam de qualibet lingua, qui cum propria lingua scirent linguam Chaldaicam, ut possent sibi legere atque exponere litteras gentium universarum. Imo regibus qui diversarum nationum scripta recipiunt, tales sunt opportuni. Et ut ait Hieronymus, De facili esse non potuit, ut essent in regis palatio, et linguæ regis essent ignari. Præterea in Scholastica historia dicitur, et ex Hieronymo sumptum est, quod lingua Chaldæa eadem est cum Syra, propinqua Hebrææ. Philo autem disertissimus Judæorum, dixit linguam Hebræam et Chaldaicam esse eamdem, eo quod Abraham Hebræus, fuit Chaldæus. Cui scriptura ista obviare videtur : si enim eadem esset, pueri isti in Hebræo idiomate prompti, Chaldæum idioma non didicissent. Ideo solvit Glossa, et est glossa Hieronymi, quod forte secundum quorumdam opinionem, Abraham utramque noverat linguam, sed filios suos atque familiam non docuit nisi linguam Hebræam.
paras.en: [[1:4|that he might teach them|Ut doceret eos]], that is, the aforesaid master of the eunuchs, by himself or rather through others under him, [[1:4|the learning|litteras]] [Latin *litteras*, "letters"], that is, the sciences, [[1:4|and tongue of the Chaldeans|et linguam Chaldæorum]]. Now the letters of the Chaldeans were chiefly about the sciences of divination, according to Albert. So Nabuchodonosor wished to have about him some men of every tongue who, besides their own tongue, knew the Chaldean, so that they could read and explain to him the writings of all nations. Indeed such men are useful to kings who receive writings from different nations. And as Jerome says: It could hardly be that they should be in the king's palace and ignorant of the king's tongue. Moreover, it is said in the *Scholastic History*, and it is taken from Jerome, that the Chaldean tongue is the same as the Syrian, and near to the Hebrew. But Philo, the most eloquent of the Jews, said that the Hebrew and Chaldean tongues are the same, because Abraham the Hebrew was a Chaldean. This passage of Scripture seems to go against him: for if it were the same, these boys, ready in the Hebrew idiom, would not have had to learn the Chaldean. So the Gloss (and it is a gloss of Jerome's) resolves it: perhaps, as some hold, Abraham knew both tongues, but taught his sons and household only the Hebrew.

paras.t: Et constituit eis rex annonam, id est refectionem, per singulos dies de cibis suis, et de vino unde bibebat ipse : ut abundanter de necessariis corporis provisi, studio fructuosius liberiusque vacarent. Sollicitudo namque temporalium, impedit studii integritatem. Voluit quoque rex eos tam delicate nutriri, ut pulchriores, gratiosioresque essent : ut scilicet regio cibo sanguis optimus nutriretur, et spiritus qui aptus esset ad virtutis atque scientiæ informationem. Vinum quoque pretiosum moderanter sumptum, optimum facit spiritum et optimum motum, secundum Albertum. Verumtamen, quoniam tam laute vescentes, communiter in quantitate et qualitate excedunt, et delectationem exquirunt; frequenter contingit ut ad studium scientiæ ac virtutum ineptiores reddantur, qui eis vescuntur. Ut enutriti præfata annona vinoque regio, et etiam lingua ac litteris Chaldæorum, tribus annis, postea starent in conspectu regis Nabuchodonosor, ad ejus obsequium prompti, et digni adstare tanto regi.
paras.en: [[1:5|And the king appointed them a daily provision|Et constituit eis rex annonam]], that is, their fare [Denis puts this gloss on *annonam*, "provision", before *per singulos dies*, "daily"], [[1:5|of his own meat, and of the wine of which he drank himself|de cibis suis, et de vino unde bibebat ipse]]: so that, abundantly provided with the body's necessities, they might give themselves to study more fruitfully and freely. For anxiety about temporal things hinders wholeness of study. The king also wished them to be fed so delicately that they might be more handsome and more gracious: that is, so that by the royal food the best blood might be nourished, and a spirit apt to be formed in virtue and knowledge. Precious wine too, taken in moderation, makes the best spirit and the best motion, according to Albert. Yet since those who feed so sumptuously commonly exceed in quantity and quality, and seek after pleasure, it often happens that those who eat such food are made less fit for the pursuit of knowledge and virtue. [[1:5|that being nourished|Ut enutriti]] by the aforesaid provision and the royal wine, and also by the tongue and letters of the Chaldeans, [[1:5|three years, afterwards they might stand before the king|tribus annis, postea starent in conspectu regis]] Nabuchodonosor, ready for his service and worthy to stand before so great a king.

paras.t: Fuerunt inter eos de filiis Juda, Daniel, Ananias, Misael, et Azarias. De diversis gentibus plures pueri gratiosi fuerunt intra palatium regis inducti, inter quos isti quatuor præclariores fuerunt : an vero de filiis Israel non erant nisi hi quatuor introducti, non est adeo certum. Porro, ut refert Hieronymus, aiunt Hebræi hos quatuor fuisse eunuchos sive castratos, impleta in eis prophetia Isaiæ ad Ezechiam : Tollent, scilicet Babylonii seu Chaldæi, de semine tuo, et facient eunuchos in domo regis Babylonis. Unde et Josephus adstruit quod rex eos castravit : quod et aliis gentibus a se vastatis fecisse dignoscitur, ut in Scholastica fertur historia. Sed istud Hieronymus aliqualiter reprobare videtur, quoniam pueri isti dicuntur sine macula exstitisse; castratio autem est maxima macularum, propter quod in Deuteronomio legitur : Non intrabit eunuchus amputatis vel attritis testiculis vel abscisso veretro ecclesiam Domini. Hinc, secundum Albertum et Lyram, eunuchi dicuntur ratione obsequii, non castrationis. Glossa quoque hic ait : Non videntur abscissi, qui sine macula sunt. Quidam enim eunuchizantur aut vi, aut infirmitate; quidam autem se castrant pro cœlesti patria, et hi abscissi non sunt nisi sua voluntate, et hi sunt sine macula. Unde in Matthæo loquitur Christus : Sunt eunuchi, qui de matris utero sic nati sunt; et sunt eunuchi, qui facti sunt ab hominibus; et sunt eunuchi, qui se castraverunt propter regnum cœlorum. Secundum hoc igitur sensus est, quod pueri isti actu castitatis, fideique custodia, non corporis sectione, eunuchi dicuntur. Denique regis industria pueros corpore speciosos, et mente perfectos elegit : quoniam sicut virtus mentis substantialis est felicitati, sic corporis pulchritudo condecorat eamdem. Propter quod in primo Ethicorum habetur : Non dicitur felix, qui specie corporis turpissimus est. Juventus quoque et pulchritudo se mutuo ornant, et amabiliores efficiunt. Juvenes quippe, ceteris paribus, naturaliter amabiliores consistunt. Unde Philosophus asserit, quod delectatio ornat felicitatem, quemadmodum pulchritudo juventutem.
paras.en: [[1:6|Now there was among them of the children of Juda, Daniel, Ananias, Misael, and Azarias.|Fuerunt inter eos de filiis Juda, Daniel, Ananias, Misael, et Azarias]] Many comely youths of divers nations were brought into the king's palace, and among them these four were the most eminent; but whether these four alone of the children of Israel were brought in is not altogether certain. Further, as Jerome relates, the Hebrews say that these four were eunuchs, that is, castrated men, so that the prophecy of Isaias to Ezechias was fulfilled in them: [[Is 39:7|they shall take away|Tollent]] (that is, the Babylonians or Chaldeans) of thy seed, and shall make them eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon [so Denis; in Isaias the words run: they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon]. Hence Josephus too affirms that the king castrated them, as he is known to have done also to other nations that he laid waste, as is related in the Scholastic History [that is, the Historia scholastica of Peter Comestor]. But Jerome seems in some measure to reject this, since these youths are said to have been without blemish, and castration is the greatest of blemishes; for which reason we read in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 23:1|An eunuch, whose testicles are broken or cut away, or yard cut off, shall not enter into the church of the Lord.|Non intrabit eunuchus amputatis vel attritis testiculis vel abscisso veretro ecclesiam Domini]] Hence, according to Albert and Lyra, they are called eunuchs by reason of their office, not of castration. The Gloss too says here: They do not seem to have been cut who are without blemish. For some are made eunuchs either by force or by infirmity; but some castrate themselves for the heavenly country, and these are not cut except by their own will, and these are without blemish. Hence Christ says in Matthew: [[Matt 19:12|there are eunuchs, who were born so from their mothers womb: and there are eunuchs, who were made so by men: and there are eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven|Sunt eunuchi, qui de matris utero sic nati sunt; et sunt eunuchi, qui facti sunt ab hominibus; et sunt eunuchi, qui se castraverunt propter regnum cœlorum]]. According to this, then, the sense is that these youths are called eunuchs by the practice of chastity and the keeping of faith, not by any cutting of the body. Lastly, the king with care chose youths comely in body and perfect in mind: for as virtue of mind belongs to the substance of happiness, so beauty of body adorns it. For which reason it is said in the first book of the Ethics [of Aristotle]: He is not called happy who is most ugly in bodily appearance. Youth also and beauty adorn each other and make men more lovable; for the young, other things being equal, are by nature more lovable. Hence the Philosopher asserts that pleasure adorns happiness as beauty adorns youth.

paras.t: Et imposuit eis præpositus eunuchorum nomina alia quam ante habebant, scilicet nomina linguæ Chaldææ, quæ sibi honorabiliora videbantur quam nomina linguæ Hebrææ. Danieli imposuit nomen Balthasar. Circa quod in Scholastica historia dicitur : Balthasar erat nomen regii generis, quod rex Danieli imposuit, quia de ejus adoptione jam cogitavit, ut Epiphanius protestatur. Ex quibus etiam constat, quod præpositus de regis præcepto nomina permutavit, sicut et Pharao in Ægypto aliud nomen imposuit Joseph. Et Ananiæ imposuit nomen Sidrach ; Misaeli, Misach ; Azariæ, Abdenago. Secundum Albertum, Balthasar interpretatur, capillus capitis : unde propter judicii subtilitatem sic dictus est Daniel. Sidrach interpretatur, decorus meus : sicque vocatus est Ananias pro decore virtutis et corporis. Misach interpretatur, qui scit risus, vel, de gaudio : et ita appellatus est Misael, quoniam bona jucunditate commanentes fecit jucundos, implens illud ad Romanos : Qui ministrat, in hilaritate. Ministrantibus nempe hilaritas competit. Abdenago interpretatur serviens taceo : sicque nuncupatus est Azarias, quoniam sine contradictione et murmure deservivit, quod ministrantibus congruit.
paras.en: [[1:7|And the master of the eunuchs gave them names|Et imposuit eis præpositus eunuchorum nomina]] other than those they had before, namely names of the Chaldean tongue, which seemed to him more honourable than names of the Hebrew tongue: [[1:7|to Daniel, Baltassar|Danieli imposuit nomen Balthasar]]. On which it is said in the Scholastic History: Balthasar was a name of the royal house, which the king gave to Daniel because he was already thinking of adopting him, as Epiphanius attests. From this it is also plain that the master changed their names by the king's command, as Pharao too in Egypt gave Joseph another name[[Gen 41:45||]]. And [[1:7|to Ananias, Sidrach|Ananiæ imposuit nomen Sidrach]]; [[1:7|to Misael, Misach: and to Azarias, Abdenago|Misaeli, Misach ; Azariæ, Abdenago]]. According to Albert, Balthasar is interpreted "hair of the head": and so Daniel was called for the fineness of his judgement. Sidrach is interpreted "my comely one": and so Ananias was called for the comeliness of his virtue and of his body. Misach is interpreted "he that knoweth laughter", or "of joy": and so Misael was named, because by his good cheerfulness he made those who lived with him cheerful, fulfilling that word to the Romans: He that ministereth, [[Rom 12:8|with cheerfulness|in hilaritate]] [so Denis; in the Epistle it is he that sheweth mercy who does so with cheerfulness, while ministering is spoken of in Rom 12:7]. For cheerfulness befits those who minister. Abdenago is interpreted "serving, I am silent": and so Azarias was called, because he served without gainsaying or murmuring, which befits those who minister.

paras.t: Proposuit autem Daniel in corde suo, ne pollueretur de mensa regis, neque de vino potus ejus, id est, ne regiis alimentis contra legem Dei sui vescendo peccaret. Peccatum autem animæ, est animæ macula atque pollutio. Potuitque quatuor modis peccatum istud accidere. Primo, si comederet prohibitum lege, ut carnes porcinas. Secundo, si comederet injuste acquisita, ut rapta sive extorta, juxta illud Proverbiorum : Comedunt panem impietatis, et vinum iniquitatis bibunt. Tertio, si comederet de idolothyto, id est idolis immolato, quod in prima ad Corinthios Apostolus prohibet, ne scandalizentur infirmi. Etenim antiquitus mos fuit, in mensa magnorum aliquam poni portionem de oblationibus idolorum. Quarto, crapulose seu superflue comedendo, quomodo in mensis regum fieri solet. Præsertim autem in vino regnat luxuria. Ideo secretariis regum abundans vini usus non competit, prout in Proverbiis inducitur : Noli vinum dare regibus, quia nullum secretum ubi regnat ebrietas. Porro sobrietas victus ad sapientiæ adeptionem disponit, sicut in Ecclesiastico habetur : Proposui a vino abstrahere carnem meam, ut animum meum transferrem ad sapientiam. Propter quod rursus Salomon ait : Qui amat vinum et pinguia, non erit sapiens. Prædictum vero abstinendi propositum, non Daniel tantum, sed et tres socii ejus conceperunt, secundum Albertum, Scholasticamque historiam. Solus tamen Daniel tanquam principalior nominatur.
paras.en: [[1:8|But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not be defiled with the king's table, nor with the wine which he drank|Proposuit autem Daniel in corde suo, ne pollueretur de mensa regis, neque de vino potus ejus]]: that is, that he would not sin by eating the king's food against the law of his God. For the sin of the soul is the soul's stain and defilement. And this sin could have come about in four ways. First, if he ate what the law forbade, such as swine's flesh[[Lev 11:7||]]. Secondly, if he ate what had been unjustly gotten, such as things seized or extorted, according to that of Proverbs: [[Prov 4:17|They eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of iniquity|Comedunt panem impietatis, et vinum iniquitatis bibunt]]. Thirdly, if he ate of an idolothyte, that is, of what had been sacrificed to idols, which the Apostle forbids in the first Epistle to the Corinthians[[1 Cor 8:4||]], lest the weak be scandalized. For it was the custom of old for some portion of the offerings made to idols to be set on the tables of the great. Fourthly, by eating gluttonously or to excess, as is wont to be done at the tables of kings. And above all, wantonness reigns in wine. Therefore an abundant use of wine does not befit the counsellors of kings, as is set down in Proverbs: [[Prov 31:4|give not wine to kings|Noli vinum dare regibus]], [[Prov 31:4|because there is no secret where drunkenness reigneth|quia nullum secretum ubi regnat ebrietas]]. Moreover, sobriety of diet disposes a man to the attaining of wisdom, as we have in Ecclesiasticus [so Denis; the words are from Ecclesiastes]: I purposed [[Eccles 2:3|to withdraw my flesh from wine, that I might turn my mind to wisdom|a vino abstrahere carnem meam, ut animum meum transferrem ad sapientiam]]. For which reason Solomon says again: [[Prov 21:17|he that loveth wine, and fat things|Qui amat vinum et pinguia]], shall not be wise [the Vulgate has: shall not be rich]. Now this purpose of abstaining was conceived not by Daniel alone but also by his three companions, according to Albert and the Scholastic History. Yet Daniel alone is named, as the chief among them.

paras.t: Circa hunc locum scribit Hieronymus : Qui de mensa regis et vino ejus non vult accipere ne polluatur, si sapientiam atque doctrinam Babylonis sciret esse peccatum, non acquiesceret discere quod non liceret. Discunt autem ipse et tres pueri illam, non ut sequantur, sed ut reprobent, judicent et convincant : quomodo si quispiam adversus mathematicos velit scribere imperitus mathematicorum, risui pateret; et adversus philosophos disputans, si nesciat dogmata philosophorum. Discunt ergo ea mente doctrinam Chaldaicam, qua Moyses sapientiam Ægyptiorum. — Verumtamen agnoscendum, quod in doctrinis Chaldæorum multa falsa, superstitiosa ac impia de divinationibus aliisque vanitatibus continebantur : quæ scire, peccatum non fuit; nec discere ea ob finem prætactum, fuit illicitum.
paras.en: On this place Jerome writes: He who will not take of the king's table and of his wine, lest he be defiled, would not have consented to learn what was not lawful, if he had known the wisdom and learning of Babylon to be sinful. He and the three youths learn it, then, not to follow it, but to reprove, judge and refute it: just as, if anyone unskilled in the mathematicians [that is, the astrologers] wished to write against them, he would be laughed at; and so too one disputing against the philosophers, if he does not know the teachings of the philosophers. They learn the Chaldean learning, therefore, with the same mind with which Moses learnt the wisdom of the Egyptians. — Yet it must be acknowledged that the teachings of the Chaldeans contained many false, superstitious and impious things about divinations and other vanities: to know these was no sin, nor was it unlawful to learn them for the end just mentioned.

paras.t: Et rogavit Daniel eunuchorum præpositum, ne contaminaretur, id est, ne cogeret se de prædictis comedere contra legem. Ita et Judith renuit vesci de cibariis Holofernis.
paras.en: [[1:8|and he requested the master of the eunuchs that he might not be defiled|Et rogavit Daniel eunuchorum præpositum, ne contaminaretur]]: that is, that he would not force him to eat of the said things against the law. So too Judith refused to eat of the meats of Holofernes[[Jdt 12:2||]].

paras.t: Dedit autem Deus Danieli gratiam, id est acceptabilitatem et gratiositatem, et misericordiam, id est miseriæ relevamen seu compassionem, in conspectu, id est in interioribus oculis, principis eunuchorum : ita quod Deus fecit Danielem acceptabilem principi, movens cor principis ad complacentiam Danielis propter virtutes quas vidit in eo; itemque ad compatiendum eidem propter malum suæ captivitatis, et quia de regia fuit stirpe. Hinc ait Hieronymus : Præposuerat Daniel regiis epulis viles suos cibos, idcirco gratiam et misericordiam in conspectu principis eunuchorum accepit, Domino largiente. Ex quo intelligimus pro necessitate rerum, si quando sancti ab infidelibus diliguntur, Dei esse misericordiæ, non bonitatis hominum perversorum.
paras.en: [[1:9|And God gave to Daniel grace|Dedit autem Deus Danieli gratiam]], that is, acceptableness and favour, [[1:9|and mercy|et misericordiam]], that is, relief of his misery, or compassion, [[1:9|in the sight|in conspectu]], that is, in the inward eyes, [[1:9|of the prince of the eunuchs|principis eunuchorum]]: so that God made Daniel acceptable to the prince, moving the prince's heart to take pleasure in Daniel because of the virtues he saw in him, and also to feel for him because of the evil of his captivity, and because he was of the royal stock. Hence Jerome says: Daniel had preferred his own poor fare to the king's dishes; therefore he received grace and mercy in the sight of the prince of the eunuchs, the Lord bestowing it. From which we understand that, as the need of things requires, if ever the saints are loved by unbelievers, it is of God's mercy, not of the goodness of perverse men.

paras.t: Et ait princeps eunuchorum ad Danielem, et per eum etiam ad socios ejus, pro quibus sicut pro se ipso Daniel intercessit : Timeo ego dominum meum regem Nabuchodonosor. Quasi dicat : Quum diligam te, quantum in me est, libenter te exaudirem; sed regem meum formido, quia transgredientibus sua præcepta non parcit. Qui constituit vobis cibum et potum. Qui si viderit vultus vestros macilentiores præ ceteris adolescentibus coævis vestris, id est vultibus eorum, condemnabitis caput meum regi, id est, occasio eritis quod me occidet, tanquam sibi rebellem. Nam ut in Proverbiis scribitur, Indignatio regis, nuntii mortis. Rursusque Salomon fatetur : Sicut fremitus leonis, ita ira regis; et sicut ros super herbam, etc. Recte etiam dixit præpositus, Coævis vestris : quia si essent seniores aut juniores, forte non esset æqualis vis nutritiva in eis.
paras.en: [[1:10|And the prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel|Et ait princeps eunuchorum ad Danielem]], and through him to his companions too, for whom Daniel interceded as for himself: [[1:10|I fear my lord, the king|Timeo ego dominum meum regem]] Nabuchodonosor. As if to say: Since I love thee, I would gladly hear thee as far as lies in me; but I dread my king, for he does not spare those who transgress his commands. [[1:10|who hath appointed you meat and drink|Qui constituit vobis cibum et potum]]: [[1:10|who if he should see your faces leaner than those of the other youths, your equals|Qui si viderit vultus vestros macilentiores præ ceteris adolescentibus coævis vestris]], that is, than their faces, [[1:10|you shall endanger my head to the king|condemnabitis caput meum regi]]: that is, you will be the occasion of his killing me as a rebel against him. For as is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 16:14|The wrath of a king is as messengers of death|Indignatio regis, nuntii mortis]]. And again Solomon declares: [[Prov 19:12|As the roaring of a lion, so also is the anger of a king: and his cheerfulness as the dew upon the grass|Sicut fremitus leonis, ita ira regis; et sicut ros super herbam]], etc. The master also rightly said, [[1:10|your equals|Coævis vestris]]: for if the others were older or younger, perhaps the nourishing power in them would not be equal.

paras.t: Et dixit Daniel ad Malasar, quem constituerat princeps eunuchorum super Danielem, Ananiam, Misaelem, et Azariam. Siquidem his quatuor tanquam notabilioribus præpositus ille specialem adhibuit procuratorem. Mediæ autem dignitatis est, quibusdam præesse, et quibusdam seu cuidam subesse, sicut ait Centurio : Ego homo sum sub potestate constitutus, etc.
paras.en: [[1:11|And Daniel said to Malasar, whom the prince of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Ananias, Misael, and Azarias|Et dixit Daniel ad Malasar, quem constituerat princeps eunuchorum super Danielem, Ananiam, Misaelem, et Azariam]]. For that master set a special steward over these four, as the more notable. Now it belongs to a middle rank to be over some and under others, or under one, as the centurion says: [[Matt 8:9|I also am a man subject to authority|Ego homo sum sub potestate constitutus]], etc.

paras.t: Tenta nos, obsecro, servos tuos, id est, experimentum sume de nobis, diebus decem, et dentur nobis legumina ad vescendum, et aqua ad bibendum. Hæc enim lege non vetabantur. Et contemplare, id est, corporali oculo diligenter adspice, vultus nostros, et vultus puerorum qui vescuntur cibo regio; et sicut videris rationabile esse et tibi expediens, sic facias cum servis tuis : id est, si interim videris nos aliis exiliores, precem nostram non audias ; si vero videris nos ceteris æqualiter meliusve in vultu dispositos, permitte nos in abstinentia et parsimonia ista. In hoc quod vicibus repetitis se suosque collegas subministros præfati nominat servos, captat benevolentiam ejus, et humilitatem suam declarat. Insuper legumina postulando et aquam, precem suam exaudibilem fecit : talia enim facillime acquiruntur. Itemque dicendo, Decem diebus, omnia ad Decalogum refert : discretioneque utitur, quoniam tempus hoc nec nimis longum est, ut rationabiliter denegetur; nec nimis breve, ut in eo veritas comprobetur. Porro aqua atque legumina, alimenta sunt frigida, in quibus nec gulæ neque luxuriæ concitetur voluptas. Postremo, quod Daniel a præposito eunuchorum obtinere nequivit, a substituto petivit : in quo instantia desiderii ac fervor devotionis suæ patescit. Et ut ait S. Hieronymus, in verbis his incredibilis magnitudo fidei Danielis ostenditur, quod non solum corpulentiam sibi esu vilioris cibi polliceretur, sed et tempus constituere novit. Non est ergo temeritatis, sed fidei, ob quam regias dapes contempserat. Hinc dicit Glossa, quod non temeritate, sed fidei magnitudine, tempus præfixit. Presbyteri vero in libro Judith temere statuerunt tempus tradendi se Holoferni, nisi infra quinque dies eis auxilium daretur de cœlo : idcirco a Judith sunt reprehensi.
paras.en: [[1:12|Try, I beseech thee, thy servants|Tenta nos, obsecro, servos tuos]], that is, make a trial of us, [[1:12|for ten days|diebus decem]], [[1:12|and let pulse be given us to eat, and water to drink|et dentur nobis legumina ad vescendum, et aqua ad bibendum]]; for these were not forbidden by the law. [[1:13|And look upon|Et contemplare]], that is, behold carefully with the bodily eye, [[1:13|our faces, and the faces of the children that eat of the king's meat|vultus nostros, et vultus puerorum qui vescuntur cibo regio]]: [[1:13|and as thou shalt see|et sicut videris]] it to be reasonable and expedient for thee, [[1:13|deal with thy servants|sic facias cum servis tuis]]: that is, if in the meantime thou seest us thinner than the others, do not grant our prayer; but if thou seest us as well or better disposed in countenance than the rest, let us keep to this abstinence and frugality. In calling himself and his colleagues, the fellow-servants of the said master, servants again and again, he wins his good will and shows his own humility. Moreover, by asking for pulse and water he made his prayer one that could be granted: for such things are very easily got. Again, by saying *Ten days* he refers all to the Decalogue; and he uses discretion, since this time is neither so long that it might reasonably be refused, nor so short that the truth could not be proved within it. Further, water and pulse are cold foods, in which the pleasure neither of gluttony nor of lust is stirred up. Lastly, what Daniel could not obtain from the master of the eunuchs he asked of his deputy: in which the earnestness of his desire and the fervour of his devotion appear. And, as St Jerome says, in these words an incredible greatness of Daniel's faith is shown, in that he not only promised himself plumpness from eating poorer food, but also knew how to fix the time. It is therefore not of rashness but of faith, the faith for which he had scorned the king's dishes. Hence the Gloss says that he fixed the time not rashly but by the greatness of his faith. But the elders in the book of Judith rashly fixed a time for giving themselves up to Holofernes unless help were given them from heaven within five days[[Jdt 7:25||]]: for that reason they were rebuked by Judith[[Jdt 8:10||]] [the margin gives Ibid. vii, 10 et seq.; Judith's rebuke begins at Jdt 8:10].

paras.t: Qui audito sermone hujuscemodi tam rationabili, tentavit eos diebus decem. Post dies autem decem apparuerunt vultus eorum meliores et corpulentiores præ omnibus pueris qui vescebantur cibo regio : et id gratiæ potius quam naturæ est adscribendum, quanquam sanitas animæ et corporis sit sobrius cibus. Vigilia autem, et tortura, et cholera viro infrunito, ut dicitur in Ecclesiastico. Porro sancti delectatione virtutis etiam corporaliter per redundantiam reficiuntur, atque interna eis a Deo infusa jucunditas, in corpus redundat. Propter quod scriptum est : Animus gaudens ætatem floridam facit; spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa.
paras.en: [[1:14|And when he had heard these words|Qui audito sermone hujuscemodi]], so reasonable, [[1:14|he tried them for ten days|tentavit eos diebus decem]]. [[1:15|And after ten days, their faces appeared fairer and fatter than all the children that ate of the king's meat|Post dies autem decem apparuerunt vultus eorum meliores et corpulentiores præ omnibus pueris qui vescebantur cibo regio]]: and this is to be ascribed to grace rather than to nature, although sober food is the health of soul and body; but [[Ecclus 31:23|Watching, and choler, and gripes, are with an intemperate man|Vigilia autem, et tortura, et cholera viro infrunito]], as is said in Ecclesiasticus [the margin gives Ecclus. xxx, 23; the verse is Ecclus 31:23]. Further, the saints are refreshed even in body by the delight of virtue overflowing into it, and the inward gladness poured into them by God overflows into the body. For which reason it is written: [[Prov 17:22|A joyful mind maketh age flourishing: a sorrowful spirit drieth up the bones|Animus gaudens ætatem floridam facit; spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa]].

paras.t: Porro Malasar tollebat, haud dubium quin occulte, ne perciperetur a rege, cibaria, et vinum potus eorum, quæ scilicet eis fuerant deputata, convertens ea in proprios usus, dabatque eis legumina.
paras.en: [[1:16|So Malasar took|Porro Malasar tollebat]] (no doubt secretly, lest it be noticed by the king) [[1:16|their portions, and the wine that they should drink|cibaria, et vinum potus eorum]], that is, what had been allotted to them, turning it to his own uses, [[1:16|and he gave them pulse|dabatque eis legumina]].

paras.t: Pueris autem his dedit Deus scientiam et disciplinam, de quarum distinctione prædictum est, in omni libro quem addiscebant, legebant seu exponebant, et in omni sapientia, id est notitia divinorum : quo enim se amplius disposuerunt ad illuminationes divinas, eo copiosius sunt desuper illustrati ; et quo carnalia oblectamenta plenius contempserunt, carnemque ab illicitis represserunt, eo ad spirituales consolationes et supernaturales instructiones, digniores inventi sunt. Propter quod scriptum est in Sapientia : Sapientia facile videtur ab his qui diligunt illam, et invenitur ab eis qui quærunt illam; præoccupat eos qui se concupiscunt. Et in Isaia : Quem docebit scientiam? et quem intelligere faciet auditum? Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere. Porro, secundum Hieronymum, Deus contulit pueris istis scientiam et disciplinam sæcularium litterarum, ut cuncta quæ legebantur intelligerent, et spiritu Dei de Chaldæorum scientia judicarent.
paras.en: [[1:17|And to these children God gave knowledge, and understanding|Pueris autem his dedit Deus scientiam et disciplinam]] [*scientia* and *disciplina*: "knowledge" and "learning"; the Douay-Rheims renders *disciplina* "understanding"], of the distinction between which we have spoken above, [[1:17|in every book|in omni libro]] that they learned, read or expounded, [[1:17|and wisdom|et in omni sapientia]] [Denis reads: and in all wisdom], that is, the knowledge of divine things: for the more fully they disposed themselves for divine illuminations, the more abundantly were they enlightened from above; and the more completely they despised carnal delights and restrained the flesh from unlawful things, the worthier were they found of spiritual consolations and supernatural instruction. For which reason it is written in Wisdom: Wisdom [[Wis 6:13|is easily seen by them that love her, and is found by them that seek her|facile videtur ab his qui diligunt illam, et invenitur ab eis qui quærunt illam]]; [[Wis 6:14|She preventeth them that covet her|præoccupat eos qui se concupiscunt]]. And in Isaias: [[Is 28:9|Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand the hearing? them that are weaned from the milk, that are drawn away from the breasts|Quem docebit scientiam? et quem intelligere faciet auditum? Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab ubere]]. Further, according to Jerome, God bestowed on these youths knowledge and learning in secular letters, so that they understood all that was read, and by the Spirit of God judged the learning of the Chaldeans.

paras.t: Danieli autem intelligentiam omnium visionum et somniorum, id est, Danieli tanquam sanctiori præ ceteris, data est illuminatio altior, scilicet intelligentia, seu clara cognitio omnium visionum et somniorum, tam sibi quam aliis exhibitorum, ita quod horum significationem intellexit atque exposuit. Itaque nomine visionis innuitur revelatio seu ostensio occultorum magis clara et intellectualis; tam in vigilia quam in raptu et ecstasi facta; per somnium vero, revelatio facta in somno per imaginarias formas magis obscure. Hinc Rabbi Moyses dicit, quod somnium est casus a prophetia : quoniam prophetia est visio in lumine intelligentiæ; somnium autem, manifestatio futurorum in imagine, ubi cadit et quasi occumbit lumen intelligentiæ. Dicit autem Albertus, quod visio est in qua res ut futuræ sunt, ostenduntur. Hieronymus autem hic ait : Daniel ultra tres pueros hoc habebat insigne, quod visiones et somnia, quibus per symbola quædam et ænigmata monstrantur futura, sagaci mente cernebat : ut quod alii videbant in phantasmate, hic oculis cordis adspiceret.
paras.en: [[1:17|but to Daniel the understanding also of all visions and dreams|Danieli autem intelligentiam omnium visionum et somniorum]]: that is, to Daniel, as holier than the rest, a higher illumination was given, namely understanding, or clear knowledge, of all visions and dreams, shown both to himself and to others, so that he understood their meaning and expounded it. So by the name of vision is meant a revelation or showing of hidden things that is clearer and intellectual, made whether in waking or in rapture and ecstasy; but by dream, a revelation made in sleep through imaginary forms, more obscurely. Hence Rabbi Moyses [that is, Maimonides] says that a dream is a falling-off from prophecy: for prophecy is a vision in the light of the understanding, but a dream is a showing of things to come in an image, where the light of the understanding falls and as it were sinks down. And Albert says that a vision is that in which things are shown as they will be. And Jerome says here: Daniel had this distinction beyond the three youths, that with a keen mind he discerned visions and dreams, in which things to come are shown through certain symbols and riddles: so that what the others saw in a phantasm, he beheld with the eyes of the heart.

paras.t: Completis itaque diebus trium annorum, post quos dixerat rex ut introducerentur coram se : qui interim eruditi fuerunt et digni effecti adsistere regi; introduxit eos princeps eunuchorum in conspectu Nabuchodonosor, ut eorum eruditionem experiretur. Quumque eis locutus fuisset rex, eos examinando, quæstiones atque ænigmata proponendo : sicut regina Saba tentasse legitur Salomonem; non sunt inventi tales, id est tam sapientes, de universis coram rege adductis, ut Daniel, Ananias, Misael, et Azarias. Gratiæ enim lumen, omnino efficacius est lumine naturali; et qui a Spiritu Sancto instruuntur, his qui humanitus informantur sapientiores refulgent. Ideo ait Psalmista : Beatus homo quem tu erudieris, Domine.
paras.en: [[1:18|And when the days were ended|Completis itaque diebus]] of the three years, [[1:18|after which the king had ordered they should be brought in|post quos dixerat rex ut introducerentur]] before him (in the meantime they had been taught and made fit to stand before the king), [[1:18|the prince of the eunuchs brought them in before Nabuchodonosor|introduxit eos princeps eunuchorum in conspectu Nabuchodonosor]] [a note in the edition gives *præpositus*, "master", as in the Vulgate, for *princeps*], so that he might test their learning. [[1:19|And when the king had spoken to them|Quumque eis locutus fuisset rex]], examining them, putting questions and riddles to them, as the queen of Saba is read to have tried Solomon[[3 Kings 10:1||]], [[1:19|there were not found|non sunt inventi]] [[1:19|such|tales]], that is, so wise, [[1:19|among them all|de universis]] who were brought before the king, [[1:19|as Daniel, Ananias, Misael, and Azarias|ut Daniel, Ananias, Misael, et Azarias]]. For the light of grace is altogether more effective than the light of nature, and those who are taught by the Holy Ghost shine out wiser than those who are formed by human means. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 93:12|Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord|Beatus homo quem tu erudieris, Domine]] [the margin gives Ps. xcii, 12; the verse is Ps 93:12].

paras.t: Et steterunt in conspectu regis, parati ad respondendum et obsequendum in licitis et honestis. Et omne verbum sapientiæ, quantum ad divina, et intellectus, id est interpretationis seu expositionis dubiorum ac difficilium, quod sciscitatus est ab eis rex, invenit in eis decuplum super cunctos ariolos et magos qui erant in universo regno ejus, id est multo plus quam in aliis, ita quod promptius, sapientius, evidentiusque ad omnia responderent. Et ponitur hic numerus determinatus pro indeterminato, quum dicitur, Decuplum, sicut in Psalmo : Memor fuit verbi sui, quod mandavit in mille generationes; et in Job, En decies confunditis me. Quod etiam in Apocalypsi fit sæpius. Porro arioli nominantur, qui de occultis vaticinantur, per sacrificia in aris idolorum oblata : talis fuit Balaam. Magi vero dicuntur astrologi, qui per constellationes judicant de futuris atque occultis. Tamen, secundum Hieronymum, magi quasi magni dicuntur, qui de omnibus philosophantur. Hujusmodi vero artes divinandi inter Chaldæos vigebant : quas pueri isti secuti non sunt, sed per inspirationem divinam melius sunt locuti, quam per divinationes Chaldæi.
paras.en: [[1:19|and they stood in the king's presence|Et steterunt in conspectu regis]], ready to answer and to obey in things lawful and honourable. [[1:20|And in all matters of wisdom|Et omne verbum sapientiæ]] [literally: every word of wisdom], as regards divine things, [[1:20|and understanding|et intellectus]], that is, of the interpretation or exposition of doubtful and difficult things, [[1:20|that the king enquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the diviners, and wise men, that were in all his kingdom|quod sciscitatus est ab eis rex, invenit in eis decuplum super cunctos ariolos et magos qui erant in universo regno ejus]]: that is, much more than in the others, so that they answered all things more readily, more wisely and more clearly. And here a definite number is put for an indefinite one, when it says *ten times*, as in the Psalm: [[Ps 104:8|He hath remembered|Memor fuit]] his word, [[Ps 104:8|which he commanded to a thousand generations|quod mandavit in mille generationes]]; and in Job: [[Job 19:3|Behold, these ten times you confound me|En decies confunditis me]]. This is done often in the Apocalypse too[[Apoc 5:11||]][[Apoc 7:4||]]. Now those are called diviners who prophesy of hidden things by sacrifices offered on the altars of idols [*arioli*, "diviners", as if from *aræ*, "altars"]: such was Balaam. And the magi [Douay-Rheims: wise men] are the astrologers, who judge of things to come and of hidden things by the constellations. Yet according to Jerome they are called magi as if *magni*, "great" [a note in the edition gives *magistri*, "masters"], who philosophize about all things. Such arts of divination flourished among the Chaldeans: these youths did not follow them, but spoke better by divine inspiration than the Chaldeans by divinations.

paras.t: Fuit autem Daniel usque ad annum primum Cyri regis. Hoc intelligendum non est, quod non vixerit nisi usque ad primum annum Cyri regis, quoniam infra capitulo decimo scribit sibi factam desuper revelationem tertio Cyri anno. Itaque intelligendum est, quod usque illud tempus fuit in dignitate, gloria et honore, primo in Chaldæa, deinde in Media et Perside, prout in prosecutione libri patebit. Sicque competit ei illud Sapientiæ, Honestavit illum in laboribus suis. Et propter sapientiam sibi divinitus datam fuit sic exaltatus, juxta illud Sapientiæ : Propter hanc habebo claritatem ad turbas, et honorem apud seniores juvenis; et acutus inveniar in judicio, et in conspectu potentium admirabilis ero, et facies principum mirabuntur me.
paras.en: [[1:21|And Daniel continued even to the first year of king Cyrus|Fuit autem Daniel usque ad annum primum Cyri regis]]. This is not to be understood as if he lived only to the first year of king Cyrus, since below, in the tenth chapter, he writes that a revelation was made to him from above in the third year of Cyrus[[Dan 10:1||]]. So it is to be understood that up to that time he was in dignity, glory and honour, first in Chaldea, then in Media and Persia, as will appear in the course of the book. And so that word of Wisdom fits him: [[Wis 10:10|made him honourable in his labours|Honestavit illum in laboribus suis]]. And he was thus exalted because of the wisdom given him from God, according to that of Wisdom: [[Wis 8:10|For her sake I shall have glory among the multitude, and honour with the ancients, though I be young|Propter hanc habebo claritatem ad turbas, et honorem apud seniores juvenis]]: [[Wis 8:11|And I shall be found of a quick conceit in judgment, and shall be admired in the sight of the mighty, and the faces of princes shall wonder at me|et acutus inveniar in judicio, et in conspectu potentium admirabilis ero, et facies principum mirabuntur me]].

paras.t: Præterea aliquid de mystico intellectu hujus capituli inserendo, pensandum est super illud, Partem vasorum domus Dei asportavit in domum dei sui, quod vasa designant animas pretiosas, quæ virtutes continent atque scientias : quæ instigante diabolo, vicissim de Ecclesia et corpore Christi mystico, seu congregatione electa, transferuntur in habitationem mundi, ita quod relicta justitia, moribus impiorum conformantur, et vasa dæmonum fiunt, juxta illud Isaiæ : Auferetur paxillus de loco fideli, et frangetur, et cadet. Quod maxime fit, dum Joakim, id est impius, præsidet, utpote prælatus aut princeps negligens et injustus, sub quo pereunt subditi, juxta illud Ecclesiastici : Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus ; et qualis est rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea. Frequenter quoque contingit occasione præsidentium injustorum, subditos temporaliter tribulari, corporaliterque affligi, spoliari, capi, transferri, quemadmodum Daniel ejusque socii atque Ezechiel cum Joakim rege translati fuerunt. Sed hoc sapientissimus, justus, ac pius omnium Dominus ordinavit et convertit in majus bonum electorum suorum, qui etiam omni peccato non carent. Unde per talia hic purgantur, ad gratiam disponuntur, salubriter exercentur, a vitiis retrahuntur, conformanturque Christo, et cœlesti appropiant regno : qui si tempore persecutionis patientes et Deo fideles cum Daniele permanserint, maximis gratiæ donis divinitus ditabuntur, dabitque eis Dominus gratiam coram persecutoribus suis.
paras.en: Further, to add something on the mystical sense of this chapter: on the words [[1:2|part of the vessels of the house of God|Partem vasorum domus Dei]] [[1:2|he carried them away|asportavit]] [[1:2|to the house of his god|in domum dei sui]], we should consider that the vessels signify precious souls, which hold virtues and knowledge: and these, at the devil's prompting, are now and again carried off from the Church and the mystical body of Christ, that is, the chosen congregation, into the dwelling of the world, so that, forsaking justice, they are conformed to the ways of the wicked and become vessels of demons, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 22:25|shall the peg be removed|Auferetur paxillus]] from the sure place, [[Is 22:25|and it shall be broken and shall fall|et frangetur, et cadet]]. This happens most of all while Joakim, that is, the wicked man, presides: a negligent and unjust prelate or prince, under whom his subjects perish, according to that of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:2|As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers: and what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein|Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus ; et qualis est rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea]]. It often happens too, through unjust rulers, that their subjects are troubled in temporal things, afflicted in body, despoiled, taken captive and carried away, as Daniel and his companions, and Ezechiel, were carried away with king Joakim. But the most wise, just and loving Lord of all ordained this and turned it to the greater good of his elect, who are not without all sin either. Hence by such things they are here purged, disposed for grace, wholesomely exercised, drawn back from vices, conformed to Christ, and brought near to the heavenly kingdom: and if in the time of persecution they remain patient and faithful to God with Daniel, they will be enriched by God with the greatest gifts of grace, and the Lord will give them grace before their persecutors.

paras.t: Denique, secundum Glossam, vasa sunt libri philosophicalium doctrinarum, qui quidem nunquam in toto falsi sunt, sed aliqua continent vera : omnis autem veritas est a Deo, ideo non in toto, sed in parte in Sennaar, quod interpretatur mendacium, transferuntur. Hinc ait Hieronymus : Si cunctos philosophiæ revolvas libros, necesse est ut in his reperias aliquam partem vasorum Dei, aliquas scilicet veritates : ut apud Platonem, fabricatorem mundi ; et apud Zenonem Stoicorum principem, inferos immortalesque animas. Sed quia jungunt mendacium veritati, et bonum naturæ perdunt multis malis, ideo pars vasorum fertur translata.
paras.en: Again, according to the Gloss, the vessels are the books of the philosophical teachings, which are never wholly false but contain some truths; and all truth is from God: therefore they are carried into Sennaar, which is interpreted "falsehood", not wholly but in part. Hence Jerome says: If thou turn over all the books of philosophy, thou must needs find in them some part of the vessels of God, that is, some truths: as in Plato, the maker of the world, and in Zeno, the chief of the Stoics, the underworld and immortal souls. But because they join falsehood to truth, and spoil the good of nature with many evils, therefore only a part of the vessels is said to have been carried away.

paras.t: Insuper, per hoc quod rex Babylonis jussit introduci juvenes gratiosos, mente et corpore elegantes, ac eruditos, admonetur ut ad curam animarum et in Ecclesiam introducantur, qui donis gratiæ decorantur, habituque mentis et corporis perficiuntur, qui et linguam sciant eorum quorum suscipiunt curam, ut possint eos instruere. Propter quod in Exodo habetur : Provide de omni plebe viros potentes et timentes Deum, et qui oderint avaritiam, et constitue eos tribunos et centuriones.
paras.en: Moreover, by the king of Babylon's commanding that comely youths be brought in, graceful in mind and body, and learned, we are admonished that those should be brought into the cure of souls and into the Church who are adorned with the gifts of grace and made perfect in the habit of mind and body, and who also know the tongue of those whose care they take up, so that they can instruct them. For which reason we have in Exodus: [[Ex 18:21|provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God|Provide de omni plebe viros potentes et timentes Deum]], [[Ex 18:21|and that hate avarice, and appoint of them rulers of thousands, and of hundreds|et qui oderint avaritiam, et constitue eos tribunos et centuriones]].

paras.t: At vero per hoc quod Nabuchodonosor rex constituit pueris instruendis annonam, ut liberius discerent, docentur ecclesiastici viri, quibus præbendæ constitutæ sunt, ut studio vacent Scripturæ ac laudi divinæ. Etenim in sui damnationem, Christi sumit annonam, qui opus propter quod instituta est præbenda, non perficit. Propter quod in Ezechiele indignis pastoribus infructuosisque prælatis Dominus ait : Lac comedebatis, et lana operiebamini ; gregem autem meum non pavistis, et quod infirmum fuit non consolidastis.
paras.en: But by king Nabuchodonosor's appointing a provision for the youths who were to be taught, that they might learn more freely, churchmen for whom prebends [that is, the fixed incomes of cathedral and collegiate clergy] have been appointed are taught to give themselves to the study of Scripture and to the divine praise. For he takes the provision of Christ to his own damnation who does not do the work for which the prebend was founded. For which reason the Lord says in Ezechiel to unworthy shepherds and unfruitful prelates: [[Ezech 34:3|You ate the milk, and you clothed yourselves with the wool|Lac comedebatis, et lana operiebamini]]; [[Ezech 34:3|but my flock you did not feed|gregem autem meum non pavistis]], [[Ezech 34:4|The weak you have not strengthened|quod infirmum fuit non consolidastis]].

paras.t: Postremo elucescit ex præinductis, quantum abstinentia, refrenatio voluptatis, parsimonia victus, vita quieta, libertasque spiritus, ad sapientiam valeant desuper obtinendam. Renuat igitur anima nostra in carnalibus consolari, omnibusque terrenis dona Spiritus Sancti præponat, carnem cum vitiis et concupiscentiis quotidie crucifigens.
paras.en: Lastly, it is clear from what has been set out how much abstinence, the bridling of pleasure, frugality of diet, a quiet life and freedom of spirit avail for obtaining wisdom from above. Let our soul therefore refuse to be comforted in carnal things[[Ps 76:3||]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxvi, 3; the words echo Ps 76:3, My soul refused to be comforted], and set the gifts of the Holy Ghost before all earthly things, daily crucifying the flesh [[Gal 5:24|with the vices and concupiscences|cum vitiis et concupiscentiis]].

2.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : IN ANNO SECUNDO REGNI NABUCHODONOSOR.
2.title_en: Exposition of the second chapter: In the second year of the reign of Nabuchodonosor.

paras.t: In anno secundo regni Nabuchodonosor, vidit Nabuchodonosor somnium. Sicut ex præhabitis innotescit, in hoc volumine Danielis decem visiones continentur, in quibus vel ipse aliquid vidit, vel visa ab aliis explanavit. Prima est de statua grandi, quam lapis abscissus de monte sine manibus, comminuit et contrivit.
